newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to fine state firms for high wages.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to fine state firms for high wages.

text.p: The Bulgarian cabinet decided on Monday to impose fines and extra taxes on loss-making state enterprises that pay unjustifiably high wages in a bid to curb budget spending in line with IMF requirements.

"The cabinet decided to propose to parliament to amend the Profit Tax Law so funds allocated to pay wages higher than the margin be taxed as profit instead of investment," a government spokeswoman told reporters.
The International Monetary Fund and the government failed last week to agree on a budget deficit after data showed some big state loss-making firms in March raised wages 30 percent in dollar terms.

Prime Minister Ivan Kostov urged some 20 big state owned companies, which include the largest refinery, Neftochim, the Bulgarian Telecommunications Co, the National Electricity Co, to cut monthly wages in line with IMF recommendations to curb budget spending and deficits.

The Profit Tax Law amendment will be voted on by parliament later this month. Under a cabinet decree approved on Monday, employers who do not observe wage payment rules will be fined the equivalent of 25 minimum wages. The minimum wage in May was 41,300 levs.

The measures will help the government cut the deficit to around four percent, nearer the IMF-required 3.8 percent of GDP, said a government official. Work on the budget with the IMF is expected to be completed on Tuesday, the official said.
